title: A logarithm is an exponent
summary: Flip the curve y = b^x over the line y = x and you get the logarithm curve.
alt: Graphs of y = b to the power x and y = log base b of x, mirror images over the line y = x, with one point on each.

ex.label: Exponential
ex.text: y = b to the power x.

lg.label: Logarithm
lg.text: y = log base b of x.

steps.title: An exponential curve
steps.narration: The blue curve is \( y = {{b|int}}^x \). Each x (the **exponent**) gives a y (the **power**).

steps.title: One point on it
steps.narration: At \( x = {{n|int}} \) the curve is at \( y = {{b|int}}^{{{n|int}}} = {{N|2}} \). So the blue point is \( ({{n|int}}, {{N|2}}) \).

steps.title: Flip it over
steps.narration: A **logarithm** asks the question the other way round: \( {{b|int}}^{?} = {{N|2}} \). Swap x and y: the red curve is \( y = \log_{{{b|int}}} x \), the blue curve flipped over the dashed line y = x.

steps.title: The log is the exponent
steps.narration: The red point is \( ({{N|2}}, {{n|2}}) \), so \( \log_{{{b|int}}} {{N|2}} = {{n|2}} \). **A logarithm is an exponent.**

steps.title: Special values
steps.narration: At \( n = 0 \): \( {{b|int}}^0 = 1 \), so \( \log_{{{b|int}}} 1 = 0 \). The red curve crosses the x-axis at 1.

steps.title: Negative exponents
steps.narration: At \( n = -1 \): \( {{b|int}}^{-1} = \frac{1}{{{b|int}}} \), so the log is negative for numbers below 1.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.narration: Slide **n** and switch the **base**. Read both the power and the log.

formulas.title: The link
formulas.text: Same three numbers, written two ways.

formulas.title: Two special logs
formulas.text: Because b to the power 0 is 1 and b to the power 1 is b.

challenges.title: Change the form
challenges.prompt: Which statement means the same as \( 5^2 = 25 \)?
challenges.hint: The base stays the base. The exponent becomes the log.

challenges.title: Log of 1
challenges.explain: \( 2^0 = 1 \), so \( \log_2 1 = 0 \). This is true for every base.

intro: Powers and logarithms are two ways of writing the same fact.
takeaways: b^n = N is the same as log_b N = n.
The two curves are mirror images over y = x.

notes.title: Why only bases 2 and 3 here?
notes.text: They keep the numbers small enough to draw. Base 10 (common logs) is on the next animation.
